phases.title: Story: chapters 1–4
phases.blurb: Play the campaign clean through Chapter 4. These trophies are automatic, so bank them and learn the map while there is no pressure.

phases.title: Mid-game contacts
phases.blurb: Start the stranger strands as they appear, and let story choices register while the campaign is still open. Only a finished chain counts, so carry each one to its finale.

phases.title: Activities & collectibles
phases.blurb: The widest phase. Clear every activity category once, then pick three card sets and one stunt loop.

phases.title: Crime & chaos
phases.blurb: Heists, robberies and the combat stunts. Plan routes, bank cash and keep manual saves before timed encounters.

phases.title: Exploration & spending
phases.blurb: Sweep the map, register vehicles, buy garages and shops. Most of this overlaps with WAiNK check-ins.

phases.title: Endgame & cleanup
phases.blurb: Finish the story, close out 100% and collect the platinum. Save before the finale if you care about missables.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum has no challenge of its own: it lands the moment the other 54 trophies are on your profile, so it is a routing problem rather than a skill test. Work the six phases in order, let story travel do double duty as exploration and vehicle discovery, and leave the 100% tracker for the end so the remaining checklist is short and visible. Keep a manual save before the finale and before any choice-heavy mission, and a missed moment never costs a full replay.
steps: Follow the phases in order: story first, then strands, activities, crime, exploration and cleanup.
Let long drives and story travel tick exploration, WAiNK check-ins and vehicle discovery at the same time.
Keep a manual save before story choices, timed encounters and the final mission.
Finish the 100% tracker last; the platinum arrives with your final outstanding trophy.
trophies.tip: When a counter stalls, check the in-game stats screen before repeating anything. Most grinds record progress silently.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: This is the tutorial mission, so it comes with the opening hours and cannot be skipped or missed. Play it at a relaxed pace and let the prompts walk you through movement, driving and the first firefight. The award appears after the closing scene and the mission summary, not when the last objective clears, so give the game a moment before checking your profile.
steps: Start the campaign and follow the first objective markers.
Finish Gone Fishing through to its closing scene.
Wait for the mission summary and the trophy notification.
trophies.tip: Do not skip the opening cutscenes on a first run. They teach the controls the rest of the campaign assumes.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Clear every Chapter 1 story mission and the trophy arrives at the chapter break. Side jobs and collectibles do not move the chapter forward, so if no story marker is showing, open the mission list instead of driving around looking for icons. This is also the point where the map starts to open up, which makes it a good moment to bank a manual save and take stock of the strands that have appeared.
steps: Follow the main story markers through Chapter 1.
Complete the mission that closes the chapter.
Leave optional content until the chapter trophy appears.
trophies.tip: Chapter breaks are natural save points. Keep one here before branching into side content.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Chapter 2 ends on a story mission, and finishing that closer is what triggers the trophy. Push the campaign in order rather than jumping between side strands, because chapter-gated contacts will still be there afterwards. If you believe the chapter is done but the award has not appeared, the pause menu's story panel lists the missions still open, which is quicker than re-walking old ground.
steps: Continue the campaign into Chapter 2.
Clear the chapter missions, including the closer.
Confirm the chapter transition before detouring into side content.
trophies.tip: Use the chapter break to upgrade weapons and bank cash. The heists ahead are easier with better gear.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Chapter 3. The trigger is the chapter's closing mission, not a completion percentage, so a focused story run is the fastest route. By now the map is wide open and side content is competing for attention, but the chapter trophy only cares about the critical path. Rack up a manual save at the start of the chapter so a failed set piece does not repeat the whole run.
steps: Advance the campaign into Chapter 3.
Finish the chapter's mission chain.
Watch for the chapter-complete screen and the trophy.
trophies.tip: Keep a save at the chapter boundary so you can replay a favourite set piece without redoing everything before it.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: The last of the four chapter trophies. Complete Chapter 4's story missions through to the closing job; only that closer triggers the award. With the whole state unlocked it is tempting to wander, but the chapter trophy will not arrive until the story thread is finished, so clear it first and come back for the side content with the trophy already banked.
steps: Play the Chapter 4 main missions in order.
Complete the chapter-closing mission.
Return to strands and activities once the trophy appears.
trophies.tip: Chapter 4 is a good moment to finish weapon challenges and stock armour before the endgame begins.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The gold for finishing the main story. The finale is a point of no return for some contacts and choices, so make a manual save before you launch it and clean up anything you care about first. Once the endgame sequence finishes, the trophy is yours; there is no alternate-ending condition attached to this one. Keep the save even afterwards so you can revisit the ending without a full replay.
steps: Make a manual save before starting the final mission.
Complete the endgame sequence from start to finish.
Check the post-game state and your trophy list.
trophies.tip: Do cleanup before the finale. Some contacts and choices stop being available once the story closes.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a main-story mission, so this unlock is automatic and has no hidden condition. Reach it by following the campaign and complete its objectives; failing simply puts you back at a checkpoint. The trophy lands after the mission summary, so wait for that screen rather than restarting the console if the notification is a few seconds late. Nothing in free roam feeds into it, so there is no reason to detour before finishing the mission.
steps: Progress the story until Breakfast Run is offered.
Complete the mission's objectives.
Let the closing scene play out so the trophy registers.
trophies.tip: If the mission is not on the map, finish the current story job first. Story missions unlock in sequence.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: A story heist rather than a free-roam robbery. The Cartel Heist sits on the campaign path and awards the trophy when its last objective is cleared. You do not need a flawless stealth run or a particular crew setup for this one, only a completed mission. Prep steps count as part of the job, so finish them before you launch the finale, or you will be restarting more than you need to.
steps: Reach The Cartel Heist through the main story.
Complete the heist's setup and finale.
Stay through the escape until the mission summary appears.
trophies.tip: Do not leave the area early. The mission only counts once the results screen has loaded.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a required story mission, so the trophy is automatic and has no hidden conditions. Follow the markers, finish the mission and let the results screen load before checking your profile. If you are cleaning up other trophies at the same time, this is a good mission to keep a manual save beside, simply because story missions are the easiest content to replay.
steps: Advance the campaign to Child's Play.
Complete the mission from start to finish.
Wait for the trophy before moving on.
trophies.tip: Story missions can be replayed from the pause menu, but only the first completion awards the trophy.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Finish Headliners in the main story. It is another campaign-path trophy with no side requirements, so keep following the story thread and it will appear once its prerequisites are done. There is no score, collectible or optional objective feeding into it. If the notification does not show immediately, give the console a few seconds; trophies can lag behind the mission banner.
steps: Progress the story until Headliners unlocks.
Complete the mission and its closing scene.
Give the game a moment if the trophy does not pop immediately.
trophies.tip: Do not restart anything before the notification appears. The award is usually just behind the mission summary.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing VCIA Takedown, the airport story mission. Follow the campaign rather than trying to trigger it in free roam. The trophy appears at mission end, after the escape, not at the shootout, so play the whole sequence through. Airport missions often restrict your loadout, so read the briefing and bring what it expects instead of relying on a favourite weapon.
steps: Reach VCIA Takedown through the story.
Complete every objective, including the escape.
Wait for the mission summary.
trophies.tip: Bring the loadout the briefing expects. Airport missions can strip weapons you were counting on.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory, a late campaign mission. Like the other story trophies it has no optional conditions: push the main story until it appears and see it through. It is a long mission, so refill armour and ammo before you start rather than failing near the end. If you do fail, use the checkpoint rather than restarting the chapter from the top.
steps: Follow the campaign to Operation Savage Glory.
Complete the mission from start to finish.
Let the end-of-mission sequence play out.
trophies.tip: Late-story missions are checkpointed. Retry from the checkpoint instead of restarting the whole chapter.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's strand. His jobs unlock as you spend time with him, so clear the earlier requests before expecting the finale. The trophy is tied to the last mission only, not to a friendship meter or a side activity. If Andy has gone quiet, advance the main story or let a day pass in-game; strands like his often gate on chapter progress rather than on a timer alone.
steps: Start Andy's strand when it appears on the map.
Complete each preceding job in the chain.
Finish the final mission to close out the strand.
trophies.tip: If Andy has gone quiet, advance the main story or wait a day in-game. Strands often gate on chapter progress.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's storyline. Work through his earlier missions as they become available, then complete the finale. The trophy arrives when that last mission ends, so there is no separate collectible or activity to chase. Partial progress in the strand is worth nothing for the award, so finish his chain before starting another contact's jobs. If a mission refuses to appear, advance the main story a beat and recheck the map; these chains gate on chapter progress.
steps: Meet Kenton and complete his opening jobs.
Follow the strand through every mission.
Complete the final mission.
trophies.tip: Keep a save before the final mission of any contact strand. It is the cleanest way to replay a set piece.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's final mission. His strand opens through story progress and side contact, so finish his earlier jobs first. The trophy is awarded at the close of the chain, not for simply meeting him. Contact strands can stall while you are in the middle of another mission, so finish the current job before expecting the next call or marker. Do not ignore a strand for too long either; a few of them quietly stop offering jobs once the story moves past them.
steps: Unlock Billy's strand through story progress.
Complete every job in his chain.
Finish the final mission.
trophies.tip: Finish the mission you are on before expecting the next call. Strands pause while other jobs are active.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight different stranger strands across Leonida. Each strand is a short chain for an eccentric local, and only a finished chain counts. Partial progress in ten strands is worth less than eight completed ones, so pick a set of contacts and see each one through. Spread them across the state so the travel doubles as exploration, and recheck the map at night, when some markers appear.
steps: Find stranger markers and start each strand.
Finish every mission in a strand before moving on.
Keep a list of completed strands so you do not lose track across chapters.
trophies.tip: Some strangers only appear at certain times of day. If a marker will not spawn, come back at night or after another chapter.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission. Clear his earlier jobs as they appear, then see the last one through. There is no alternate requirement beyond finishing the chain, so do not go looking for extra objectives. If Randy is not calling, check the stranger icons on the map and make sure you have no other contact mission open; a stalled strand usually means another job is holding the slot.
steps: Start Randy's strand.
Complete the preceding missions.
Finish the finale.
trophies.tip: If a contact mission is not appearing, check the stranger icons on the map rather than only the story markers.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's storyline. Work through his available jobs first, then complete the finale when it appears. The trophy unlocks as soon as that mission ends, so there is no follow-up job to wait for. Keep an eye on the map between jobs: contact icons can move between districts, and driving to the old marker will look like the strand has vanished.
steps: Meet Tyrone and begin his strand.
Complete each job in order.
Finish the final mission.
trophies.tip: Contact icons can move between districts. Recheck the map instead of returning to the last marker.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Take Bret's request to hunt a specific unique animal and bring it down. Follow his directions to the right region, track carefully and make a clean kill. A wounded animal can lead you on a long chase, so aim for a decisive shot rather than firing at movement. Bring the rifle the request suggests and scan for tracks; rushing through brush usually spooks the target before you see it.
steps: Accept Bret's hunting request.
Travel to the indicated region and track the animal.
Take it down with a clean shot and confirm the kill.
trophies.tip: Bring the rifle the request suggests and scan for tracks. Rushing through brush spooks the target.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: This one tracks decisions made across the campaign, so it comes naturally if you engage with the story rather than rushing the markers. There is no correct morality to pick: the trophy counts choices, not which side you chose. Keep a manual save before every major decision and before the final mission, because choices are permanent and some close off later scenes. If it has not appeared mid-campaign, keep playing; it usually lands after a choice-heavy chapter.
steps: Make story choices as you play rather than skipping prompts.
Keep a manual save before every major decision.
Check the trophy after a choice-heavy chapter; it usually lands mid-campaign.
trophies.tip: There is no need to pick a specific morality. The trophy counts decisions made, not which side you chose.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Land 250 stunts anywhere in Leonida. The game counts repeatable ramps and jumps, so you do not need 250 unique locations. Pick a launch spot near a garage or safehouse, use a fast and stable vehicle, and loop it; the counter is what matters, not variety. Check the stats page every so often, because a jump that lands flat may not register and you can lose a whole session to a bad ramp.
steps: Find a ramp or jump that reliably registers a stunt.
Use a fast, stable vehicle and repeat the run.
Check the stats counter every 25 jumps to confirm progress.
trophies.tip: A stunt only counts when the game shows its name or a stunt bonus. A jump that lands flat may not register at all.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try one attempt from each activity category. You do not need to win or finish; a single completed attempt is enough. Treat it as a tour of the state: racing, fishing, the shooting range, drone racing, bowling, the arcade and the stranger activities each have their own category. Some categories only appear after certain chapters, so if the list looks short, come back to it later rather than assuming you have them all.
steps: Open the activity list and note each category.
Complete one short attempt in every category.
Recheck for categories you skipped, especially water activities.
trophies.tip: Some categories only appear after certain chapters. If the list looks short, come back to it later.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Every Shooting Range challenge needs gold, not just a pass. Gold thresholds reward accuracy and speed together, so learn each layout before chasing a score. Once the range is unlocked, replay is free, which makes this a pure skill grind you can chip away at between other trophies. Use the weapon class each challenge expects and do not rush the first run; a clean plan beats a fast miss.
steps: Unlock the Shooting Range through the story or its map marker.
Play each challenge once to learn the target order.
Replay for gold, prioritising accuracy before speed.
trophies.tip: Use the weapon class the challenge expects. Swapping to a favourite can throw off the score target even if you shoot well.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location. Each course has its own route, so one strong drone setup is not enough; learn the corners and the checkpoint order. Only a first-place finish at that specific location counts, so keep a list as you go and do not assume a win at one course covers another. A drone with good handling and stability beats raw speed on tight indoor routes.
steps: Find each Top Fun marker and race the course once to learn it.
Pick a drone with good handling and stability.
Replay until you take first at that location, then move on.
trophies.tip: Cutting a corner too tightly can miss a checkpoint. Follow the gate sequence before you start optimising your line.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Take first place in 20 different races. Repeating one event does not count, so work through the map's race markers and tick off each venue. A fast, well-handling car covers most road races; keep a bike and a boat handy for specialist events. Check the stats page for the count rather than trusting memory, and note which disciplines you have already won so you do not redo the same course.
steps: Mark every race event you have not won on the map.
Win each event once with a vehicle suited to the discipline.
Check the stats page for the count so you do not win the same race twice.
trophies.tip: Fully upgrade a race car before the grind. Spending cash up front saves far more time than retrying in a stock vehicle.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Challenge Cal to a fishing contest and land a better catch than he does. The contest is about the quality and size of what you reel in, not the number of casts, so use bait suited to the water and be patient with the bite. Losing costs nothing but time; you can come back and retry. Do not reel on the first nibble, or the fish escapes with your bait and you waste the window.
steps: Meet Cal and start the fishing challenge.
Use bait suited to the water and cast into deeper spots.
Land a heavier or higher-quality catch than Cal before time runs out.
trophies.tip: Do not reel on the first nibble. Wait for the proper bite or the fish escapes with your bait.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Finish any arcade cabinet's game from beginning to end. You do not need a high score or a perfect run; reaching the end is the requirement. Continues are allowed where the cabinet offers them, so pick a game you can tolerate and push through. If a cabinet has several games, check which one has an ending: some are endless score attacks that can never be completed.
steps: Find an arcade cabinet with a playable game.
Play from the first level to the end.
Use continues if the cabinet allows them.
trophies.tip: If a cabinet has several games, check which one has an ending. Some are endless score attacks that cannot be completed.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Sit through a full meditation at every spot in Leonida. The spots are scattered and easy to drive past, so work region by region and mark them as you find them. A location only counts once the whole meditation completes, so do not stand up early or cancel the prompt. Approaching on foot makes the interaction prompt easier to spot, especially at lookouts and shoreline spots.
steps: Mark every meditation spot on the map.
Complete the full meditation at each one.
Recheck the region list for blanks before moving on.
trophies.tip: Meditation spots often sit on hills or shoreline lookouts. Approaching on foot makes the prompt easier to spot.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Finish three complete Collectible Card sets. Loose cards do not count; each set must be turned in whole. Pick sets whose cards overlap with places you are already visiting, track the missing pieces and complete one set at a time rather than spreading thin across six. Check whether a missing card is story-gated before you spend an evening hunting it, because some sit inside businesses or mission areas.
steps: Open the collectibles menu and pick three sets to target.
Collect every card in a set, using the map for the last few.
Turn in each complete set before starting the next.
trophies.tip: Some cards sit inside businesses or mission areas. Check whether a missing card is story-gated before hunting for it.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 different locations. It is a check-in app rather than a collectible hunt: open it wherever you are, log the spot and move on. The app records each location, so a systematic drive around the state beats wandering and hoping. Combine the loop with exploration and vehicle discovery, and you will pass dozens of eligible locations without a single detour.
steps: Open WAiNK It and check in at your current location.
Drive a route through new districts, checking in at each stop.
Use the app's map to find spots you have not logged.
trophies.tip: Combine this with exploration and vehicle discovery. You will pass dozens of eligible locations without detouring.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's challenges. They range from timed trials to combat and driving tests, and any challenge counts toward the total. Pick the types you are good at first, then grind the remainder; the counter is cumulative across the whole state. Some challenges only unlock after story progress, so a short list does not always mean you have finished everything available.
steps: Open the challenges list and sort by type.
Complete the short, repeatable challenges first.
Track the count and rotate types when one becomes frustrating.
trophies.tip: Some challenges only unlock after story progress. A short list does not always mean you have finished them.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play a complete game of bowling at the Kolt & Associates alley. Rent a lane, throw a full game and let the score settle. You do not need a high score, only a completed game at this specific venue, so a few frames that clip the gutter cost you nothing but time. Other bowling alleys do not count, so travel to the right one before you start.
steps: Travel to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Rent a lane and start a full game.
Finish all frames; the score does not matter for the trophy.
trophies.tip: Use the lane guide and a straight release. A wild hook is the fastest way to turn a short game into a long one.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The description is deliberately coy: this is the partner-activity showpiece, the one built around doing something public with your companion. Bring your partner to the activity tied to the trophy, follow the on-screen prompts through the scene and let it conclude rather than cutting away early. The award lands when the sequence finishes, not when you arrive, so stay for the whole moment.
steps: Bring your partner to the partnership activity.
Follow the on-screen prompts through the scene.
Finish the sequence and let the cutscene end.
trophies.tip: Keep a save before starting. If the scene glitches or you cancel out early, you can reload instead of waiting for another chance.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Fail or fall short on a challenge, then succeed on your second attempt at the same one. Deliberately failing once is faster than waiting for a natural miss, but keep a manual save before the moment so you can retry cleanly if the game moves on. Use the retry option rather than reloading the save, because both attempts need to happen in the same run for the trophy to register.
steps: Pick a repeatable challenge or activity you can fail quickly.
Fail the first attempt on purpose.
Win or complete the second attempt at the same challenge.
trophies.tip: Do not reload after the first failure. The trophy needs both attempts in the same session, so press retry instead.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Build a four-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then lose the police and let the meter cool completely. Stay together during the escape; the trophy only fires once you are both clear. Use a fast car and a route with alleys, tunnels or underground parking rather than trying to outgun the response. Do not switch getaway vehicles in view of the police, because the pause gives them time to close the gap.
steps: Bring your partner along and raise the wanted level to four stars.
Break line of sight and drive a clean escape route.
Wait for the wanted meter to fully clear before stopping.
trophies.tip: Do not switch getaway vehicles in view of the police. The pause gives the response time to close the distance.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in quick succession with your partner while keeping the wanted level alive between jobs. Plan a route between nearby stores, avoid getting busted or wasted, and hit the third shop before the meter resets. The trophy is about the streak, not the money, so do not stop to loot every till or fight every responder. A four-door car keeps your partner covered between stops.
steps: Pick three shops close together and scout the route.
Rob the first with your partner and leave the wanted level active.
Hit the next two without being busted or losing the heat.
trophies.tip: Two-door getaway cars are a liability with a partner. Use a four-door and keep the engine running between stops.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles by getting behind the wheel of each one at least once. Cars, bikes, boats and aircraft all count. Grab anything unfamiliar you pass and check the vehicle list for gaps; variety matters, ownership does not. The rarest models tend to sit outside hotels, marinas and wealthy districts, so sweep those areas when the easy traffic models are exhausted.
steps: Check the vehicle list for undiscovered models.
Drive or pilot each new model once.
Target categories you have ignored, such as boats and aircraft.
trophies.tip: Stealing parked cars in wealthy districts is faster than waiting in traffic. Rare models often sit outside hotels and marinas.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down five enemies during a single use of Combat Focus. The count resets each time the ability ends, so all five must fall in one window. Pick a crowded fight, activate the ability when several enemies are already in view and prioritise the closest targets. Headshots end each target faster and stretch the window, so reload before activating rather than wasting the effect on an empty magazine.
steps: Find a fight with at least five enemies.
Activate Combat Focus once they are grouped in view.
Take down five before the effect expires.
trophies.tip: Headshots stretch the timer by ending each target faster. Reload before activating so you do not waste the window.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Leave VCIA without following the normal scheduled route. Drive or fly out through an unauthorised exit rather than boarding a flight. Make a manual save first; airport security and the one-off nature of the moment make this easy to fumble. A fast car through a service gate is more reliable than trying to steal a plane on the apron, and the trophy fires once you are clear of the airport boundary.
steps: Save before entering the airport.
Get airside or to a runway access point.
Leave the airport boundary without using the scheduled departure.
trophies.tip: A fast car through a service gate is more reliable than trying to steal a plane on the apron.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description points at the Rhino, the military vehicle that turns up when the heat climbs. Treat the Rhino as the objective: get to one during a high-heat encounter or its story appearance and follow the moment through to the end rather than backing off when the response escalates. Save before provoking the military, use buildings and hills for cover, and bring explosives if you plan to take one on.
steps: Trigger a military response or reach a story section with a Rhino.
Engage it with explosives or sustained heavy fire.
See the encounter through to the trophy prompt.
trophies.tip: Do not stand in the open. A Rhino main gun ends the attempt quickly, so use buildings and hills for cover.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Scout the entrance, disable what security you can and keep the getaway quiet. A loud entry voids the stealth requirement even if you escape with the goods, so treat the alarm as a failure condition. Silenced weapons and a discreet vehicle matter more than speed; a sports car idling out front attracts exactly the attention you are trying to avoid.
steps: Scout the store and note cameras, guards and exits.
Disable security and enter without raising an alarm.
Leave the area before anyone detects you.
trophies.tip: Silenced weapons and a discreet vehicle matter more than speed. A sports car idling out front attracts attention.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape cleanly from each. Plan the approach, bring the right crew and equipment, and make sure you are clear of the police before counting a job as done. The trophy tracks vaults specifically, not ordinary store robberies, so a corner shop spree will not move it. Check the stats counter between jobs to confirm each vault registered before you move on.
steps: Unlock and scout the bank jobs available on the map.
Complete each vault robbery through to a clean escape.
Check the stats counter between jobs to confirm the tally.
trophies.tip: Try the quiet approach first. A botched stealth run turns a ten-minute job into a long firefight and a lost takedown.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Ambush an armored truck, crack it open and get away with the contents. Choose a stretch of road where the escort is thin, hit it hard and leave before reinforcements arrive. The escape is part of the trophy, not an optional extra, so do not linger over the cargo. Blocking the road with a heavy vehicle keeps the truck from driving through your ambush while you work.
steps: Find an armored truck route and pick a quiet ambush point.
Stop the truck and open the cargo hold.
Escape the area before the response closes in.
trophies.tip: Block the road with a heavy vehicle so the truck cannot drive through your ambush.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the gangs. Each gang runs a different racket in a different part of the state, so work through them one at a time and confirm the job counts. A generic robbery does not qualify; it has to belong to the gang. Some operations only appear after story missions involving that gang, so advance the campaign if one is missing from the map.
steps: Identify the gangs and their operation locations.
Rob one operation for each gang.
Track the gang list and confirm each entry.
trophies.tip: Some gang operations only appear after story missions involving that gang. Advance the campaign if one is missing.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in a suitably flashy car. Pick a fast model, line up the exit and hit the front window at speed. The trophy fires once you are clear of the building, so keep the throttle down until you are outside the lot. Approach the glass straight rather than at an angle, or the car spins and you lose the run.
steps: Find a showroom with a display car you can take.
Line up the front window and accelerate.
Drive clear of the building and the lot.
trophies.tip: A supercar has the speed but can spin on the glass. Approach straight and keep the throttle pinned.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock a pedestrian down using a melee attack from a moving vehicle. Drive close, lean out and strike at low speed so the hit connects. A clean drive-by melee is all the trophy needs; there is no requirement to escape or avoid a wanted level. Low speed is the trick, because at high speed the attack misses and you end up with a wanted level instead of a trophy.
steps: Drive slowly alongside a pedestrian.
Lean out and throw a melee attack.
Confirm the hit registered and leave the area.
trophies.tip: Low speed is the trick. At high speed the attack misses and you end up with a wanted level instead.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 in marked bills through your contacts. Build up the marked cash through jobs and robberies, then run it through the laundering option until the full amount has been processed. The counter tracks money laundered, not money earned, so do not spend the marked bills first. Launder in batches as soon as you have the cash; holding marked bills until the end risks losing them in a botched job.
steps: Accumulate marked bills from jobs and robberies.
Open your contacts and start a laundering job.
Repeat until the stats page shows $250,000 laundered.
trophies.tip: Launder in batches as soon as you have the cash. Holding marked bills until the end risks losing them in a botched job.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Visit every named area across Leonida so each one registers on your map. Drive or fly through the state systematically, checking the region list for blanks, and do not forget islands and outlying districts, which are the ones most often left for last. Flying at low altitude sweeps large rural regions quickly, but land or drive through settlements so they register rather than just passing overhead.
steps: Open the map's region list and note every unvisited area.
Plan a loop through each district, including islands.
Recheck the list after the loop for missed corners.
trophies.tip: Flying at low altitude sweeps large rural regions quickly, but land or drive through settlements so they register.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Find a bar or terrace with a water view, order a drink and let the moment play out. The trophy is easy to pass by, so make a manual save before you go and do not rush the interaction. Go at sunset if you want the best screenshot; the trophy does not require a time of day, but the view is worth the wait.
steps: Travel to Ocean Beach.
Find a bar or terrace with a view of the water.
Order a cocktail and stay for the full scene.
trophies.tip: Go at sunset if you want the best screenshot. The trophy does not require a time of day, but the view is worth the wait.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness one of the game's strange encounters out in the world. These events are easy to miss, so explore at night, follow unusual map markers and investigate odd lights or sounds when they appear. The encounter has to play out for the trophy to register, so approach it rather than driving past. If nothing is spawning, try a different region or time of day; these moments are rare by design.
steps: Look for unusual markers or sounds while exploring at night.
Approach and investigate rather than driving past.
Let the full encounter play out.
trophies.tip: Keep the encounter a surprise if you care about spoilers. If you only want the trophy, sweep rural roads at night and stop for anything that looks out of place.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across the state's shops, including clothing, vehicle and property stores. The total is cumulative, so buy what you need and top up the remainder with large purchases. Do not buy and immediately resell; only money actually spent counts. Combine this with garage purchases and vehicle upgrades so the same spending also feeds the other collection trophies. The stats page keeps a running total, so check it before a big purchase to avoid overspending on things you do not need.
steps: Check your spend total in the stats page.
Buy useful gear first: armour, weapons and vehicle upgrades.
Top up the remainder with clothing or a large vehicle purchase.
trophies.tip: Combine this with vehicle discovery and garage purchases so the money does double duty for other trophies.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy every garage property available on the map. Save up the cash, purchase each one as it comes up for sale and check the property list to confirm none have been overlooked. Garages are also useful storage for the vehicles you need for other trophies, so this one pays for itself. Buy the cheap garages first so the expensive ones do not stall the whole list.
steps: Open the property list and note every garage for sale.
Buy the cheapest garages first, then save for the rest.
Recheck the list after each purchase for a missing location.
trophies.tip: Buy garages before the vehicle-discovery grind. The extra storage makes collecting rare cars far less frustrating.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 different vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Grab a range of cars, bikes and other rides, open the app for each one and add it to your list until the counter reaches ten. The vehicles do not need to be yours, so borrow whatever is nearby. Registering while you already have a wanted level still counts, which makes this an easy one to clear between jobs.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app and check which vehicles are registered.
Find a vehicle you have not registered.
Register it and repeat until the counter reads ten.
trophies.tip: Registering while you already have a wanted level still counts. Do it between jobs to save a trip.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The big one: 100% completion. The pause menu tracker splits the total into categories, and every category has to be full: story jobs, side strands, activities, collectibles and location tasks all count. Use the tracker as your checklist, clear the short categories first to shrink the list, and save the long grinds for a dedicated session. Photograph the tracker before the final push so you can spot the one activity you have been avoiding.
steps: Open the completion tracker and note every category that is not full.
Clear the short categories first to shrink the list.
Work the long grinds last, using the guide filters to avoid redoing finished content.
trophies.tip: Photograph or screenshot the tracker before the final push. It is the fastest way to spot the one activity you have been avoiding.
